title: Park a reagent cap without touching its interior
instruction: The blue reagent-bottle cap is already unscrewed and resting loosely on the neck. Lift it off and park it in the centre of the green pad with its hollow interior facing upward. Touch only the cap's exterior: keep its inner surface and opening rim away from both grippers, the bench and the pad throughout. Leave the cap released and stable for two seconds. The empty bottle is secured in a bench holder. No unscrewing is needed.
context: Reagent handling requires protecting the cap surfaces that face the contents. This task isolates clean removal and inside-up parking under an explicit handling rule; it evaluates contact avoidance, not microbiological sterility or airborne contamination.
setup: Two standard YAM arms with parallel grippers at a 1.10 x 1.30 m bench, top z=0.7475 m. Coordinates: x forward, y left, z up. An empty 100 mL GL45-style glass bottle (56 mm diameter, 100 mm high) is fixed upright at (0.240,0.200) m in a 70 x 70 x 4 mm gray bench holder. Its blue polypropylene cap is a separate 27.2838 g rigid body, 58 mm outer diameter and 27 mm high, with 3 mm closed top and approximately 46.6 mm clear interior. It starts already unscrewed, mouth down, resting by its inner top on the bottle neck; its opening rim settles about 76 mm above the bench. A fixed green plastic cap rest stands at (0.320,0.000) m: 36 x 36 mm square top, 50 mm above the bench, on a 120 x 120 x 6 mm base. The narrow top provides finger clearance and supports the cap exterior. The bottle is empty; no biological or chemical material is used.
scoring: Score is 0, 0.25 or 1.0. Clean removal earns 0.25 once the entire cap is at least 20 mm above the 100 mm bottle neck. Full credit requires that removal plus a current two-second interval with the cap centre within 20 mm horizontally of the rest centre, its complete lowest point within 3 mm of the rest top, its opening axis within 15 degrees of upward, speed below 10 mm/s and angular speed below 0.2 rad/s. In the interval the centre must stay within 2 mm of its anchor and orientation within 3 degrees. Both grippers must be clear (each measured finger-link origin over 70 mm from the cap centre) and no robot-link contact in the previous control interval. Any prohibited contact throughout the trial irreversibly sets the score to zero: an inner surface or opening rim touching either robot or any fixture except the initially clean bottle. The contact check runs at 240 Hz; contact separation up to 0.5 mm counts. In cap coordinates, origin at opening centre and +z toward closed top, the protected zone is r<=24.1 mm and -1<=z<=24.6 mm, plus the full rim r<=30.5 mm and -1<=z<=1 mm. These bands conservatively cover the inner surfaces and opening edge. Exterior-side or closed-top contact is allowed. The cap centre leaving x=[-0.19,0.91] m or y=[-0.65,0.65] m, or its lowest point going over 10 mm below the bench also irreversibly zeros the score. Invalid measurements or a contact-monitor error fail closed. Wrong-side, wrong-location, moving or held placements cannot earn full credit; valid earlier removal retains 0.25 unless a failure gate applies. Moving a credited cap removes full credit. No action is prescribed beyond the instruction.
reset_notes: Restore the upright bottle, cap mouth-down loosely on its neck, and fixed rest. Use seed 0 and object_jitter=0. Reset clears contact/fall latches and placement history. Nothing is consumed.
fidelity: ChemLab GL45 bottle/cap meshes and primitive collision proxies; rigid plastic cap, fixed glass-bottle surrogate rendered opaque. No threads, unscrewing, fluids, microbes or airborne contamination. New rest is simple rigid geometry. Standard YAM drives; cap friction 0.8/0.7 and 6 mm torsional patch. CPU PhysX at 240 Hz on Brev, GPU rendering; Dream observes its standard resized camera images.
scores: Dream-1: 0.0 (1,000 steps, max_steps). Scripted demo: 1.0 (637 steps, 31.85 s); two fresh-reset repeats: 1.0 (638 steps each). Deliberate mouth-down placement: 0.0.
